title: Ginger and treacle traybake
subtitle: a dark, sticky ginger traybake with a tender, moist crumb
excerpt: Ginger and treacle traybake is a dark, moist ginger cake made by melting butter, brown sugar, and black treacle together before beating in the eggs and flour. The treacle gives a deep, slightly bitter edge that works well against the warmth of the ginger. The batter is quite liquid when it goes into the tin and bakes to a sticky, tender traybake that keeps well.
sourceNotes: Dark treacle ginger cake is a classic British bake documented in British cookbooks from the nineteenth century onward. The melt-and-mix method is the standard technique for this style of dense, dark ginger cake.

recipe.freezeNotes: Cut into squares before freezing. Wrap individually and freeze for up to 3 months. Thaw at room temperature.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps at room temperature, covered, for up to 5 days. The flavour deepens and the crumb becomes stickier over the first 2 days.

content.text: Ginger and treacle traybake is a classic melt-and-mix ginger cake: the butter, brown sugar, and treacle go into a pan over a low heat, melt together, then get beaten up with the eggs and milk before the flour and spices are folded in. The batter is very liquid and pours easily into the tin. It bakes to a dark, sticky, slightly dense crumb that becomes more moist over the first day or two.
Heat the oven to 170 degrees C (fan 150 degrees C / gas 3). Grease and line a 30 x 20 cm rectangular baking tin.
Put the butter, brown sugar, and treacle into a medium saucepan over a low heat. Stir until the butter melts and the mixture is smooth. Remove from the heat and leave to cool for 10 minutes.

Beat the eggs and milk into the cooled treacle mixture. Pour into the bowl with the sifted flour, ground ginger, cinnamon, and bicarbonate of soda. Stir until just combined and no dry patches remain. The batter will be quite runny. Stir in the stem ginger if using.
Pour into the prepared tin and bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the top is set and a skewer comes out with just a few moist crumbs. Do not overbake; the traybake should be moist.
Leave to cool completely in the tin before cutting into squares.

attrs.problem: Sinking in the middle after baking
attrs.avoid: Avoid opening the oven in the first 25 minutes; the cold air causes the very liquid batter to sink.
attrs.fix: Do not open the oven until at least 25 minutes have passed. If the top looks well set, check with a skewer at 30 minutes.

attrs.problem: Dry and crumbly rather than sticky and moist
attrs.avoid: Avoid overbaking; treacle cakes dry out quickly past the correct baking time.
attrs.fix: Remove from the oven as soon as a skewer shows moist crumbs rather than a clean pull. The cake continues to firm up as it cools.
